name: Truncatable primes
description: A truncatable prime is a prime number which contains no zeros in decimal notation and all its suffixes are primes. 1 is considered to be not a prime. You are given a positive integer n . Figure out whether it is a truncatable prime.
input_specification: The only line of input contains an integer n ( 2 ≤ n ≤ 10 7 ).
output_specification: Output "YES" if n is a truncatable prime. Output "NO" otherwise. Quotes for clarity only.
approach_summary: Identify exchange argument or greedy choice property. Sort elements by payoff ratio or deadline and greedily pick candidates to achieve global optimum.
